title: Halden Sleep mattress catalog pre-merge audit: validate SKU roster against the authored InDesign merge template, proof-render a sample spread, and emit a fix-list report

source.reference: Flipkart and amazon Mattress Listing Setup

grounding_note: VERBATIM from the Freelancer.com brief: "The product descriptions and a clean image set are already prepared; what I am missing are the detailed specifications that Flipkart requires—sizes, materials, firmness levels, certifications, weight, packaging dimensions, and anything else their catalogue team usually checks for approval." Reframed IP-cleanly for fictional brand Halden Sleep as an InDesign catalog data-merge pre-flight AUDIT: validate the supplied SKU roster against the authored merge template + the mandatory-spec checklist, proof-render a sample spread, and emit a per-SKU fix-list report.
one_line_ask: Audit Halden Sleep's mattress product roster CSV against the authored InDesign catalog merge template and the mandatory-spec checklist, run a proof data-merge of a sample spread to inspect for blank/overset frames, and emit a per-SKU validation findings report with a prioritized fix-list.
full_brief: Halden Sleep is a boxed-mattress startup about to send its 2026 wholesale catalog to the printer and to its retail-partner intake team. We already have (a) an authored InDesign catalog template (halden_catalog_template.pdf) — a 2-up A4 landscape product-spread layout with real InDesign data-merge fields (<<sku>>, <<model>>, <<size>>, <<firmness>>, <<material>>, <<height_in>>, <<weight_lb>>, <<cert>>, <<box_dims>>, <<price>>, plus an <<image>> frame per product) and (b) a product roster CSV (mattress_roster.csv) with one row per SKU that our ops team filled in by hand. Before we spend money on a print run and before the retail intake team rejects us, we need someone to VALIDATE the roster against the template and against the marketplace-style mandatory-spec checklist — the same fields a catalogue approval team checks: size, material, firmness level, certification, weight, and packaging (box) dimensions must be present and non-blank on EVERY SKU, prices must be formatted consistently, firmness must be one of a controlled vocabulary (Soft / Medium / Medium-Firm / Firm), and specs must be consistent across all SKUs (no unit drift, e.g. some rows in cm and some in inches). Deliverable: a plain-English validation findings report (halden_catalog_audit.md/pdf) that lists, per SKU, exactly which mandatory field is missing, mis-formatted, off-vocabulary, or inconsistent, with a prioritized fix-list ranked by blocker vs. warning; plus a proof: run a data-merge of the FIRST sample spread through the authored template and export it so we can eyeball whether any merge frame comes out blank or text oversets. Do NOT redesign the catalog — the .indd layout is final; we only need the data checked and a proof spread rendered. Page size A4 landscape, 300 DPI proof. Please also confirm every referenced product image resolves (no missing/placeholder frames) by previewing the sample.

inputs.name: halden_catalog_template.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a 2-up A4 LANDSCAPE mattress-catalog product spread. Must contain REAL InDesign data-merge placeholder fields named <<sku>>, <<model>>, <<size>>, <<firmness>>, <<material>>, <<height_in>>, <<weight_lb>>, <<cert>>, <<box_dims>>, <<price>>, and a linked <<image>> frame per product, arranged as a repeating product card with a spec table. Authored by hand in InDesign so the fields actually bind; a PDF-converted .indd with literal text would NOT bind.
inputs.realism_notes: Modeled as the client's own final catalog template (normal freelancer hand-off). document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields; it is a supplied input, not a chain output. The audit checks the CSV against THIS template's field set.

inputs.name: mattress_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a realistic hand-filled product-roster CSV, ~14 rows, columns exactly: sku,model,size,firmness,material,height_in,weight_lb,cert,box_dims,price,image. Model names like 'Halden Cloud 10', 'Halden Terra Hybrid', etc. DELIBERATELY seed realistic data-entry defects a catalogue-approval team would reject: 2-3 rows with a BLANK mandatory field (e.g. empty cert or empty box_dims), 1 row with firmness off the controlled vocabulary ('Plush' instead of Soft/Medium/Medium-Firm/Firm), 2 rows with UNIT DRIFT (box_dims in cm while the rest are in inches; one height row in cm), inconsistent price formatting ('$799' vs '799.00' vs '1,299'), one duplicate SKU code, and one image cell pointing to a filename not present in the image set. The remaining rows are clean and valid.
inputs.realism_notes: The defects are the whole point of an ANALYZE task — they are what the audit must detect and report. Column headers exactly match the authored template's <<merge fields>> so the proof data-merge binds.

inputs.name: product_images_set/ (12 packshots)
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of clean e-commerce packshots of boxed foam/hybrid mattresses on plain light-grey studio seamless: some shown as the compressed box with a branded sleeve, some as the rolled-out mattress at a slight angle showing quilted top and side profile. Even soft studio light, neutral white balance, product centered, generous margin. Filenames like sku_HC10.jpg, sku_TH20.jpg matching the roster's image column (with ONE roster row intentionally referencing a filename NOT in this set).
inputs.realism_notes: Supplied 'clean image set' straight from the brief ('a clean image set are already prepared'). One deliberately-missing filename lets the audit catch an unresolved image reference during the sample preview.

inputs.name: spec_checklist.txt
inputs.gen_prompt: Write a short plain-text mandatory-spec checklist a marketplace catalogue-approval team uses for mattresses: (1) mandatory non-blank fields = size, material, firmness, cert, weight_lb, box_dims; (2) firmness controlled vocabulary = Soft, Medium, Medium-Firm, Firm; (3) all linear dimensions in INCHES, weight in POUNDS (no cm/kg); (4) price formatted as $#,###.## consistently; (5) sku must be unique; (6) every image reference must resolve. Mirrors the brief's 'sizes, materials, firmness levels, certifications, weight, packaging dimensions ... their catalogue team usually checks'.
inputs.realism_notes: The rubric the audit validates against; taken almost verbatim from the client's own field list. Keeps the pass/fail criteria objective and grounded.

outputs.name: halden_catalog_audit.pdf
outputs.spec: Plain-English validation findings report: a per-SKU table of every mandatory-field defect (blank field, off-vocabulary firmness, unit drift, inconsistent price format, duplicate SKU, unresolved image) with a prioritized fix-list split into BLOCKERS (will fail approval / export blank frame) vs WARNINGS (cosmetic/inconsistency). Rendered to PDF from the recipe note for hand-off. Also delivered as halden_catalog_audit.md: The same findings + fix-list authored as a Markdown recipe note (source of the PDF), listing each SKU, the failing rule from the checklist, and the exact edit needed.

outputs.name: proof_spread_sample.pdf
outputs.spec: Proof render of the FIRST sample product spread produced by running the authored template through a data-merge of the sample rows, A4 landscape ~300 DPI, so the client can eyeball blank/overset merge frames and a missing image placeholder before the full print run.

connector_workflow.note: Create a Creative Cloud working folder to hold the roster, template, images and audit artifacts for this catalog review.
Open an upload session for the supplied inputs (template .indd, roster CSV, checklist, 12 packshots).

connector_workflow.inputs_from: upload_session; halden_catalog_template.pdf; mattress_roster.csv; spec_checklist.txt; product_images_set/ (12 packshots)
connector_workflow.note: Finalize the upload; returns URNs the preview, merge and image-checks reference.

Inspect the authored .indd to read its merge-field set and confirm which fields the layout actually expects (<<sku>>,<<model>>,<<size>>,<<firmness>>,<<material>>,<<height_in>>,<<weight_lb>>,<<cert>>,<<box_dims>>,<<price>>,<<image>>).

Read the uploaded roster CSV (mattress_roster.csv) to enumerate every SKU and its filled/blank cells for the field-completeness pass. Uses asset_preview_file, the same read-only inspection call step 4 uses on the template: media_summarize was wrong here because it requires an AUDIO/VIDEO asset with speech and this task has no AV input at all.

Read the uploaded mandatory-spec checklist (spec_checklist.txt) — required fields, firmness vocabulary, unit and price-format rules, SKU uniqueness, image-resolves — as the rubric the roster is validated against. Inspection via asset_preview_file for the same reason as step 5: media_summarize needs speech-bearing AV.
Search the uploaded packshot set for each filename referenced in the roster's image column to detect the unresolved/missing image reference (a hit-or-miss per SKU).
Inline-preview the resolved packshots to confirm they are real product images (not blank/placeholder) so the audit only flags the genuinely-missing one.

Convert the supplied print-ready PDF template(s) (halden_catalog_template.pdf) into a real InDesign document (halden_catalog_template.indd) so the downstream merge/export steps have a genuine .indd to bind to. outputFormat='indd'.

Run a PROOF data-merge of the roster through the client's authored .indd (real <<fields>>) so we can observe how the current roster binds — blank cells surface as empty frames, over-long text as overset. NOTE: document_merge_data_layout emits ONE MERGED FILE PER CSV ROW, not a single multi-page document; the audit only needs the FIRST row's spread, which step 11 renders. [T] requires the supplied authored template; no layout is composed.
Export the first proof spread to an A4-landscape ~300 DPI PDF for visual inspection of blank/overset frames.

Author the validation findings: cross-reference every SKU against the checklist (blank mandatory field, off-vocabulary firmness, cm/kg unit drift, inconsistent price format, duplicate SKU, unresolved image) and read the rendered proof spread (proof_spread_sample.pdf) directly for its visible defects — empty spec cells, overset description, missing packshot — into a per-SKU fix-list split BLOCKERS vs WARNINGS. The proof PDF is inspected here rather than by media_summarize, which requires speech-bearing AV.

Render the Markdown findings report (halden_catalog_audit.md) to the halden_catalog_audit.pdf hand-off deliverable LOCALLY. This is a local helper, not an Adobe call: document_convert_pdf converts an EXISTING PDF into an InDesign file and cannot author a PDF from .md/.json/.txt, so the report PDF is produced by a local render of the findings file.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining. Setup: create_folders(1) -> init_upload(2) -> finalize_upload(3) yields uploaded_asset_urns, the shared source for inspection. The audit fans out from those URNs via read-only inspection: asset_preview_file(4) reads the template's real merge-field set; asset_preview_file(5) reads the roster rows; asset_preview_file(6) reads the checklist rules. The image-resolution branch chains roster_field_summary(5) -> asset_search(7) -> asset_inline_preview(8) to catch the missing packshot. The proof branch chains uploaded_asset_urns(3) + the converted template(9) + roster -> document_merge_data_layout(10) [T], which emits one merged file per CSV row, -> document_render_layout(11) exporting the FIRST row's spread as proof_spread_sample.pdf. Everything converges: roster_field_summary(5) + checklist_rules(6) + image_resolution_map(7) + packshot_thumbnails(8) + proof_spread_sample.pdf(11) all feed local_write_recipe_note(12) [L], which local_render_pdf(13) [L] turns into the PDF report. No step stands free of the chain; the two report deliverables (audit PDF, audit MD) and the proof spread PDF emerge only from the assembled pipeline. 13 calls, 9 distinct Adobe tools plus two local helpers.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon analyze task: 13 calls — 11 Adobe connector calls across 9 distinct Adobe tools in two groups (asset_* storage/search/preview inspection, document_* InDesign convert/merge/render) plus two [L] local helpers that author and render the findings report. Difficulty comes from genuinely INSPECTING heterogeneous inputs (an authored .indd's field set, a defect-seeded roster CSV, a rules checklist, a 12-image packshot set) and cross-referencing them: field completeness, controlled-vocabulary firmness, unit drift, price-format consistency, SKU uniqueness, and image resolution, THEN validating the theory by running a genuine [T] proof data-merge and visually reading the rendered spread for blank/overset frames before writing an evidence-backed per-SKU fix-list. It respects every hard limit: no generative fill / object-removal / text-to-image / upscaling / from-scratch layout; document_merge_data_layout binds and document_render_layout only EXPORTS the client's authored .indd (a supplied input); the output is a findings report + proof, exactly matching an ANALYZE deliverable.

reverify.banned_capability_check: No banned capabilities used, and no tool is asked to do something it cannot. TOOL-SEMANTICS REPAIRS: (a) media_summarize requires an AUDIO/VIDEO asset with speech and this task supplies none — the three calls that pointed it at a CSV, a TXT and a rendered PDF are gone. Steps 5 and 6 now use asset_preview_file, the same read-only inspection call step 4 already uses on uploaded assets, preserving roster_field_summary and checklist_rules for the downstream audit; the call that summarized proof_spread_sample.pdf was removed outright and the proof is now read directly by the local note-authoring step. (b) document_convert_pdf converts an EXISTING PDF into an InDesign file and cannot AUTHOR a PDF from Markdown — the final step is now local_render_pdf (server 'local', exec_mode 'L'), a local render of halden_catalog_audit.md, explicitly not an Adobe call. (c) document_merge_data_layout's note now states it emits one file per CSV row rather than a single multi-page PDF; the audit needs only the first row's spread, which document_render_layout exports. (d) local_write_recipe_note's server was corrected from 'adobe' to 'local' to match its [L] exec_mode. No image_crop_and_resize / reframe-crop, no generative fill, no text-to-image or from-scratch art/logo, no upscaling, no object-removal/inpainting. No layout is composed by the connector: document_merge_data_layout [T] binds the client's supplied authored .indd and document_render_layout only EXPORTS it.
reverify.notes: SLOT-MATCH verified: workflow_nature=analyze, output_modality=document (the audit PDF/MD report), vertical=retail_ecommerce, operation_family=Layout & Data (InDesign data-merge validation) all equal slot L10; fictional IP-clean brand Halden Sleep replaces the real Flipkart/mattress vendor. Counts after the tool-semantics repair: 13 workflow steps, 9 distinct Adobe tools (asset_create_folders, asset_initialize_file_upload, asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_preview_file, asset_search, asset_inline_preview, convert_pdf_to_indd, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout) plus two local helpers (local_write_recipe_note, local_render_pdf) that are excluded from the Adobe count. Every remaining step is in-bounds: (1) document_merge_data_layout(10) is a genuine [T] merge against a supplied authored template with real <<fields>>; CSV headers exactly match those fields, so it binds — no from-scratch layout, and it emits one file per row. (2) document_render_layout(11) only exports. (3) asset_preview_file(4,5,6), asset_inline_preview(8) and asset_search(7) are INSPECTION tools used to read/validate content, not to generate it — correct for an analyze task and the sanctioned analyze inspection palette. (4) The deliverable is a findings/report file (halden_catalog_audit.pdf/.md) plus a proof render, emitted via local_write_recipe_note(12) [L] then rendered by local_render_pdf(13) [L]. (5) All defects to be found are seeded in the supplied CSV/image set, so the audit is objectively verifiable against spec_checklist.txt. grounding_note quotes the real brief verbatim; source.platform=Freelancer.com and source.reference = the candidate title 'Flipkart and amazon Mattress Listing Setup'.
